RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday,  the February  17, 2009/Magha 28, 1930 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Civil Aviation; Corporate Affairs; Culture; Heavy Industries
and Public Enterprises; Petroleum and Natural Gas;
Tourism; Water Resources)
Total number of questions — 20
8
Satyam Computers Scam
*21. SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRA-
SEKHAR: Will the Minister of
CORPORATE AFF AIRS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether any significant headway has
been made into the Satyam Computers
Scam;
(b) if so, the details thereof, indicating
the extent of misappropriation of funds,
the period for which these irregularities have
been going on;
(c) the extent of involvement of auditors
and others in the Scam; and
(d) the steps taken/proposed to be taken
to ensure to detect other cases of profit
boosting and other corporate frauds?
Establishment of museums at district
and regional level
*22. MS. MABEL REBELLO:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of CULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to establish
more museums at district and regional levels
to take the museum movement to the people
in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also proposed to
redefine the museum concept to keep pace
with the evolving social changes;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) what are the details of districts/
regions where this new concept is proposed
to be implemented in Orissa and Jharkhand?
Transportation of oil from Caspian
region
*23. SHRIMATI VIPLOVE THAKUR:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether the issue of transportation
of oil from Caspian region through the
Mediterranean and Red Sea into India was
discussed during the visit of Foreign
Minister of Turkey to India in February,
2008;

9
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(b) if so, the salient features of the
discussion;
(c) whether it is also a fact that oil, if
brought from Caspian region through the
Mediterranean and Red Sea, will be cheaper;
(d) if so, whether Government has taken
any decision on the issue; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Aviation scene in Bihar
*24. SHRI RAJNITI PRASAD: Will
the Minister of CIVIL A VIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) the present status of expansion of
infrastructure facilities at Patna and Gaya
airports;
(b) how many more airports have been
planned for Bihar;
(c) the present status of their execution;
and
(d) whether Government would
consider expanding infrastructural facilities
and providing more air connectivity with
different countries of the world in view of
tourist influx in Gaya?
Competition among oil
companies
†*25. SHRIMATI  SUSHMA
SWARAJ: W ill the Minister of
PETROLEUM AND NA TURAL GAS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the decision
of reducing the prices of petrol and diesel
has been left on open market;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether the open market pricing
policy would increase the competition
among various oil companies; and
(d) if so, the policy formulated to
regulate the competition among these oil
companies?
Problems faced  by corporate houses
*26. SHRI SABIR ALI: Will the
Minister of CORPORATE AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of problems pointed out
and suggestions made by corporate houses
during the last two years and the current
year;
(b) the steps taken to solve these
problems;
(c) the details of problems solved and
those yet to be solved; and
(d) by when these problems would be
solved?
Exit facilities at Delhi Airport
†*27. SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
Will the Minister of CIVIL A VIA TION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it has come to light that in
the recent past the passengers have had to
wait for a long time while coming out after
the arrival of  the flights at Delhi Airport;
(b) if so, whether any arrangement has
been made by all the airlines and other
agencies for maintaining time in carrying
out all works relating to various procedures,
i.e. reaching the bus at aircraft, receiving
cargo, hiring taxi etc.; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?

10
Flaring of natural gas in
Assam
*28.  KUMAR DEEPAK DAS: Will
the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) the quantity of natural gas being
flared out daily in Assam during the last
ten years and its total cost, according to
the  present price of natural gas; and
(b) the steps taken or proposed to be
taken by Government for use of natural
gas and feasibility of gas based industries
in Assam?
Demand of oil in India
*29. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether India's oil demand is
expected to grow by 0.13 million barrel per
day (mb/d) and it tends to even out to a
certain degree by the year end;
(b) whether oil demand declined by 47
trillion barrel per day (tb/d) in October,
2008 following the highest figure of plus
200 tb/d of the year in September,
2008;
(c) whether the demand of crude in the
first quarter of 2009 may decline by
2.3 mb/d, compared to the same period last
year; and
(d) if so, the steps taken to improve
India's oil production in 2009?
 Measures for attracting foreign
tourists
*30. SHRIMATI  SUPRIYA SULE:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of TOURISM be
pleased to state:
(a) whether she  has asked State
Governments to take all possible steps at
their end to halt the slump in incoming
tourist traffic for the last few months and
has urged them to cut tax for attracting
foreign tourists;
(b) if so,  the main suggestions pointed
out to the States including increasing of
floor area ratio for hotels;
(c)  the reaction of  State Governments
thereto;
(d) to what extent State Governments
have agreed; and
(e) whether  Government  is confident
of  States attracting more foreign tourists ?
Corporate scams
*31. SHRI MOINUL HASSAN: Will
the Minister of CORPORATE AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware that
the Satyam Computers scam is just the tip
of the iceberg and that many business
houses in India, banks, auditors and
Government agencies collude with vested
interests to dress up balance sheets to
mislead investors; and
(b) if so, what steps Government
proposes to take in this regard?

11
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
CAT-III trained pilots with private
airlines
*32. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN:
SHRIMATI  SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL A VIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Directorate General of
Civil Aviation (DGCA) has recently taken
serious note of flight disruptions due to
fog despite most airlines claiming to have
CAT-III trained pilots;
(b) if so, the details of flights cancelled
or delayed due to fog during the past two
months at Indira Gandhi International
Airport (IGIA), Delhi;
(c) whether most of the private airlines
are not keen to provide training to their
pilots for CAT-II or III; and
(d) if so, the action taken by the DGCA
against private airlines which are not
providing training to their pilots for CAT-
II or III?
Compensation to contractual
employee
*33. SHRI PRAVEEN RASHTRAPAL:
Will the Minister of CIVIL A VIA TION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether his Ministry is aware about
an accidental death of a Spice Jet contractual
employee within Ahmedabad airport
runway campus;
(b) what compensation will be paid by
the said company or by civil aviation
authorities to the family of the deceased;
(c) whether his Ministry is aware that
blanket outsourcing of various jobs by the
civil aviation authority has given freedom
to private contractors to violate various
labour laws; and
(d) what action or preventive steps are
suggested by his Ministry to protect the
legitimate right of minimum wages, other
facilities, medical treatment and
compensation in case of untimely death of
workers while on duty?
Auction of Oil and Gas Blocks
*34. SHRIMATI MOHSINA
 KIDW AI:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
 BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government has decided to
launch its biggest ever auction of oil and gas
exploration blocks under New Exploration
Licensing Policy (NELP)—VIII shortly;
(b) if so, whether the Global firms have
been invited for bidding the oil and gas
exploration blocks under NELP—VIII;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether the awarding of such blocks
to companies will have any effect on the
imports of oil and gas; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Dubious functioning of Satyam
Computer Services
†*35. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the Minister of CORPORATE
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the recent
exposure of the dubious role of Satyam
Computer Services and the Price Water
House Audit company has shaken the
confidence of investors in companies;

12
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(b) if so, what is Government's reaction
thereto;
(c) whether it is also a fact that there
had been indication relating to the abovesaid
company working in a dubious manner for
many years;
(d) if so, whether Government has
chalked out any additional measures to
maintain a strict vigil on the working of
companies; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Drilling activity in Tripura
*36. SHRI MATILAL SARKAR: Will
the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware that
the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Ltd.
(ONGC) has minimized its drilling activities
in Tripura now a days causing loss of work
to the survey workers;
(b) whether it is also a fact that some of
the works of ONGC have been entrusted
to some private companies; and
(c) if so, the reasons therefor?
Strike in PSU oil companies
*37. SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether the officers of the Public
Sector Oil Companies went on an indefinite
strike in January this year;
(b) if so, the causes that led to the strike;
(c) whether demands from the striking
employees were pending to be finalized;
(d) if so, the details thereof;
(e) whether it is a fact that the wage
revision in the Oil Sector was not done
since 1997;
(f) whether Government would consider
wage revision in the Oil Sector; and
(g) if so, the details thereof?
Installation of PBNS at airports
*38. SHRI ISHWAR SINGH:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
 BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL A VIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has decided to
install Performance Based Navigational
System (PBNS) at major airports in the
country to ease traffic congestion and to
reduce risk of accidents in air;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government has conducted
preliminary tests of the system and to what
extent such system has been found
satisfactory; and
(d) the plans of Government to install
such systems at all the airports in the
country?
Medical test of foreign pilots
†*39. SHRI KRISHAN LAL
BALMIKI: Will the Minister of CIVIL
A VIA TION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Indian pilots
are frustrated due to more importance being
given to foreign pilots;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the
appointment of foreign pilots is not only
made by ignoring the company rules but
they are also posted at higher level in
management;

13
NEW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 11th February, 2009 Secretary-General.
Magha 22, 1930 (Saka)
(c) whether it is also a fact that the
foreign pilots get job in India on the basis
of medical certificates issued from USA,
Dubai and some other countries of Middle
East and are not subjected to the strict
medical fitness test as their Indian
counterparts; and
(d) the reasons for not conducting
medical fitness test of foreign pilots in
India?
Decline of foreign tourists in India
*40. PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA: Will the Min ister of
TOURISM be pleased to state:
(a) whether due to recent terrorist
attacks in several parts of the country, the
flow of foreign tourists has come down
considerably;
(b) if so, whether most of the countries
have advised their citizens not to visit India
in view of terrorist attacks;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the concrete steps taken by
Government to create confidence amongst
foreign tourists to visit India?

I N D E X
(Ministry-wise)
Civil Aviation : 24, 27, 32, 33, 38, 39,
Corporate Affairs : 21, 26, 31, 35,
Culture : 22,
Heavy Industries and Public
 Enterprises :
Petroleum and Natural Gas : 23, 25, 28, 29, 34, 36, 37,
Tourism : 30, 40.
Water Resources :—
